# cutver 0.22.0-alpha.1 — 2026-11-26

This is the first prerelease this project has cut with its own tool, and it is an alpha on purpose: the
software under test is the ladder itself. `bump` and `plan` take a channel, a prerelease promotes to the
next rung with the same flag, and `publish` can continue a release an earlier run left unfinished — on
evidence, never on a guess. Anyone who releases with `cutver` is affected by the new surfaces; plugin
authors and library consumers by the two breaking changes below. Install this one only to watch the
ladder work: `0.22.0` is the version to run in anger.

## Breaking changes

**The plugin and process drivers take the workspace root** ([#368](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/368),
[c3b7390](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/commit/c3b7390da41ace1ca28d8d1331ee9653fbf6322c)).
`PluginManager::from_config` and `from_config_with_lookup` gain a workspace-root parameter, and
`ProcessDriver::new` takes the root as its second argument.

*To migrate*: pass the workspace root to either constructor. There is no root-less constructor left, which
is the point — the root used to be ambient, and a plugin grant resolved against the wrong directory is a
permission granted over files nobody named.

**`preflight::run` and `run_supervised` changed shape** ([#363](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/363),
[5050258](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/commit/50502580556660b2129d683d0111657a972eb53a)).
`cutver::preflight::run` gains a `root: &Path` parameter, and `run_supervised` takes `dir: &Path` instead
of `Option<&Path>`.

*To migrate*: pass the root explicitly to `run`, and pass the directory itself — not an `Option` — to
`run_supervised`. The `Option` is what let a caller omit supervision without saying so.

## Prereleases are a channel, and promotion is the same flag

[#392](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/392) · [#393](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/393) ·
[ADR-0005](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/blob/main/docs/adr/0005-prerelease-channel-supersedes-0004.md)

`cutver bump --channel alpha|beta|rc|stable` (and `plan`) cuts on a ladder: a named channel appends its
identifier and starts its counter (`1.3.0` becomes `1.3.0-alpha.1`), and on a version that already carries
a prerelease the same flag **promotes** — `--channel stable` on `1.2.0-rc.1` produces `1.2.0` with no
increment. No rung is validated, so `alpha` promotes exactly like `rc`; the tool does not decide that your
alpha is too young. A request that yields the version the repository already carries releases nothing at
all — no commit, no tag, no `[publish]` command, no plugin dispatch — and says so in a `No-op` section
instead of reporting a publication that did not happen.

The bare word "channel" now always means this ladder. The CI output surface and the gate store keep their
qualifier every time they are written.

## A release can be continued instead of re-cut

[#394](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/394)

`cutver publish --resume --commit <sha>` re-enters the closing phase of a release whose steps were left
undone. It repeats only what is harmless to repeat — a tag already at the commit, a push, the floating
major tag — and it **refuses** to run a `[publish].commands` entry without a `publish-<n>` success
attestation covering that commit, naming the entry by its 1-based position. It dispatches no
`on_post_release` plugin, because that plugin may already have run.

Worth knowing before you attesting your way out of a half-finished release: the attestation **authorizes**
a repeat; it does not record that the step already ran. For a crate that already went out, attesting a
resume runs `cargo publish` a second time. The recovery for that state is re-running the asset upload and
the promotion — `docs/internals/pipeline.md` states both halves.

## The machine channel reports what it released

[#383](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/383) · [#380](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/380)

`publish` now fills `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` and the step summary the way `bump` and `plan` already did, so a
workflow stops piping a report through `jq` to learn what happened. `bump` and `plan` gained a `channel`
key computed from the version the run produced — not from the flag — so a run that promoted reports the
rung it landed on. `--verbose` forwards a process plugin's stderr to `cutver`'s own on a successful call,
which is the difference between a plugin that fails silently and one that tells you why.

## For plugin authors: a versioned envelope and a named environment

[#371](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/371) · [#370](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/370)

The invocation envelope now carries a `protocol` version, so a plugin written against one PDK and run by
another says *that* instead of failing on a field it does not recognise. The host requires it in the
request and accepts it in the answer, because the version cannot travel up any other way. A process
plugin's child also receives a named system environment baseline — twelve portable keys, applied always,
with declared grants still winning — so a plugin that read `PATH` and got nothing has a rule to point at
instead of a mystery. `cutver-pdk` **0.2.0** is published for the new envelope: a plugin built against it
rejects an older host's request with `missing field protocol`, which is the diagnosis the field exists to
produce.

## Distribution follows stable releases only

[#399](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/399) · [#398](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/398)

This project's own channels were publishing a prerelease as if it were stable. The floating major tag, the
container's `latest`, `major`, `major.minor` and `sha-` tags, the Homebrew tap and the Scoop bucket now
follow **stable releases only**, and a prerelease that skips one of them says so — in a `Stable-only`
section of the plan and outcome trees, and in a notice naming the tap and the bucket. The floating tag is
the sharp one: `uses: cutver/setup@v0` resolves to `version: latest` by default, so a tag that followed a
prerelease would have handed an alpha to everyone who asked for the default.

The package managers also stopped offering a choice nobody could make correctly: `brew install
Row0902/tap/cutver` and `scoop install cutver` now install the **plugin-enabled** build, and
`cutver-plugins` stays one more release as a deprecated shim before it goes. The lean build keeps shipping
as a release asset — on Windows x86_64 it is 1.3 MB against 5.0 MB for the plugin one, which is the whole
cost of the change and worth knowing if you install from a bucket.

## Fixes

- **A refused publish told you to do something a resume refuses** ([#398](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/398)):
  the `Fix:` line ended with "or drop `--commit` to publish the current HEAD", advice a `--resume` then
  rejects with `ResumeNeedsCommit`. The sentence now says what dropping the flag would publish on each
  path, at no extra line.
- **One `PluginManager` per publish instead of two** ([#398](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/398)):
  the resume's "left alone" line rebuilt the manager to name plugins the dispatch had already chosen.
- **A plugin's stray output cannot exhaust the host** ([#378](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/378)):
  stdout is capped at 1 MiB as a typed `AnswerTooLarge`, stderr at 64 KiB with a byte-exact marker, and the
  reader keeps draining so a loud plugin is diagnosed as an overrun rather than as a timeout.
- **A failed release no longer leaves a half-killed process tree** ([#388](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/388)):
  Windows ends the tree with one kernel call instead of a leaf-first walk that let an intermediate shell
  write past the deadline.
- **`{{ env("VAR", "default") }}` works** ([#385](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/385)): the
  documented two-argument form was shipping inside the crate and could not run.
- **A process plugin's environment grants resolve at invocation** ([#366](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/366)),
  **an external subcommand survives `ETXTBSY`** ([#379](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/379)), and
  **`doctor` reports the grants it resolves** ([#364](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/364)).
- The rest of the range is internal: test-suite seams, the source-ceiling decompositions the channel
  forced, and documentation.

## What this release does not include

- **It is an alpha, so the pipeline is the subject.** The ladder runs `alpha.1 → beta.1 → rc.1 → 0.22.0`,
  and only after the last rung is `0.22.0` the version to install. Treat a defect here as a defect in the
  ladder until proven otherwise.
- **The container image's tag set was not verified at publication.** This release's notes were written
  after the dispatch, when the image run was still in flight and the token available here lacks
  `read:packages`. The intent — `0.22.0-alpha.1` and `0.22.0-alpha.1-plugins` only — is pinned by
  `tests/container_workflow_contract.rs`, not observed.
- **`gaps 8 and 9 of [#326](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/issues/326) are still open**: declared
  per-phase needs and `--root`. Nothing in this range touches them.
- **winget is not wired.** The decision to ship one package per manager covers Scoop and Homebrew; winget
  is a new surface with its own review process and is not in this release.
- **The floating-tag skip is silent in `bump` and `--dry-run` trees.** `plan` and `publish` explain it;
  `bump` cannot without a field `src/bump/types.rs` has no room for.
- **The `#![cfg(unix)]` suites do not run on a Windows host**, so the local gate did not run them; CI's
  ubuntu and macOS legs did.
